newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Globus mulls international share issue.
newsitem.headline: Globus mulls international share issue.

text.p: Hungarian canning company Globus Rt is considering an international share offering, the firm's chief executive said on Wednesday.
"We are negotiating (about the share issue), although we are right now at a rather preliminary stage," Miklos Olah told Reuters.
Olah added that details of the share issue had not yet been decided, but that Globus expected to raise between one and three billion forints.
The money would be used to buy new canneries, he said, adding that Globus was interested in particular in the four plants Hungary's Kereskedelmi and Hitelbank (K & H) intended to sell.

K&H said last month that the four companies -- EKO, Arany Facan, SZEKO and Nagyatadi Konzervgyar -- had attracted the interest of at least three investors, each of which would like to buy all four. The bank did not name them.
Olah said: "It's not that we are all that impressed with the quality of these companies' operation, but we need capacity to expand."
In addition, Globus might also buy canneries in Beregovo, Ukraine, and Brandenburg, Germany, to help it increase its presence in other east European countries.

Olah said the new issue might or might not have voting rights. If they were voting shares, then the current biggest owner of Globus -- a consortium of German, Swiss, Austrian and Lichtensteiner investors -- might subscribe a large portion of the issue.
Globus recently began trading in Frankfurt, which Olah said would help the share issue by boosting Globus's prestige.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange, Globus closed on Tuesday at 2,055 forints.
